about.title: Mendota Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Mendota residents rely on farm equipment, tools, vehicles, and household products every day, and most work as intended. But when a product is designed poorly, manufactured with a flaw, or sold without adequate warnings, the person hurt by it often has a path to compensation without needing to prove anyone was careless. California's strict liability rules mean the focus is on the product itself, not the maker's intentions. This matters in a farming community like Mendota, where agricultural machinery, chemical handling equipment, and industrial tools are part of daily life and any defect can cause serious harm. If a defective product injured you or someone you love here, we handle these claims and can explain your options at no cost to you. There's no obligation, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
commonInjuries: Crush and amputation injuries from farm machinery
Burns from malfunctioning equipment or chemicals
Eye and respiratory injuries from unlabeled hazards
Lacerations from defective tools or blades
Electrical shock from faulty wiring or devices

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused harm. We can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. We can help figure out who was involved in getting that product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any related paperwork can be critical to building a claim. We can advise you on how to protect that evidence before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No. California generally applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you typically only need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury. This can make these claims different from a typical negligence case. We can walk you through what applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What if the product came from a farm supply store in Mendota?
items.answer: Retailers and distributors can potentially share liability along with the manufacturer, depending on how the product moved through the supply chain. This is common in agricultural communities like Mendota where equipment often passes through several hands before reaching a user. We can help sort out who may be responsible.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, manuals, or parts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may serve as key evidence. We can advise you on safely storing it until it's reviewed.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review with no obligation to move forward. If you proceed, we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
